p: The big draw near Merrion Street is the first direct Arena, the city's main concert venue, which brings in touring bands, comedians and big shows throughout the year. If your night out is built around a gig, booking your lane for a couple of hours before the doors open is a cracking way to get the evening started without having to rush.

For your visit, bring photo ID if you look young, as bar-led venues commonly ask for it. Book ahead on arena nights and weekends, when the area gets very busy. If there are more than six of you, think about booking two lanes so turns don't drag, and swap teams halfway through to keep things competitive.

Leeds Grand Theatre, home of Opera North, is close by on New Briggate and puts on musicals, plays and the ballet as well as opera. Leeds City Museum on Millennium Square is free and great for families during the day, with displays on local history and natural history.

With a bit more time, Roundhay Park on the north side of the city is a huge green space with lakes, gardens and Tropical World, a glasshouse attraction full of butterflies and exotic plants that's a favourite with kids. Kirkstall Abbey, the striking ruins of a Cistercian monastery, is another short trip out. Plenty of options for filling the day before you settle in for a night of strikes and spares.
